acceptance: A first publication writes only the remote this Cloud issues for the Project: the configured Cloud's own origin over HTTPS with the canonical project path; another environment's origin (production vs Qubits or a sibling puppyone.ai host), credentials, queries and other projects are refused; a configured HTTPS Git origin is honoured only for loopback API development.
Publishing needs a real first commit: an unborn branch (even a named one) is refused before anything is created, and a named branch with committed history passes the preflight.

A normal first push is confirmed by Git's own acknowledgement; a commit that another attempt already published counts as published; an empty Cloud main after an unresolved send lets the same commit be sent again in a fresh attempt; a different commit on Cloud main is never taken for success or overwritten.

A Cloud that is being upgraded (database_schema_outdated, schema_migration_required, service_upgrade_required) is told by its structured reason alone and the publication can resume; a message that merely sounds like one is not read as an upgrade.

A credential that cannot be verified fails closed, restores the previous configuration, and its diagnostic never carries the secret or a credential-bearing URL. The first push has its own long budget and an uncertain end is reconciled, never replayed blindly. After a failed push Cloud main is checked once: the pinned commit there is success, anything else a conflict; otherwise each refusal Cloud or Git gives is classified (contract refusal codes first, then the words of every known server: size, processing and graph budgets, HTTP 413 and request-body limits are PUSH_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, a lost connection PUSH_UNCERTAIN, an unknown code or a corrupt pack PUSH_FAILED), all retryable; an explicit size refusal names the 2 GiB limit even when Cloud main cannot be read, and Git's progress output decides nothing.

reason: TS reads Git's own push progress while uploading (share sent, bytes and rate, split across pipe chunks, redraws held to an interval but never the finish, a failing listener never reaching the push, progress lines stripped from the diagnostic) and shows the transfer under the uploading step. The native publication reports stages only: Uploading has no bytes or rate.

acceptance: Before anything needs an account a first publication prepares the folder itself: version history, a first snapshot of its files signed by the account (else Git's own identity), and a named branch, in that order and only the steps still missing, so preparing it twice changes nothing. When no identity can sign the snapshot the missing step is reported (a snapshot or a branch waits for an identity; version history does not); a new branch never takes a name a local branch has (main, puppyone-publish, puppyone-publish-2, …).
